chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Waiters' tips, Jack Johnson and Joe Louis at the Cotton Club
summary: Crawford says waiters got the tips, that Jack Johnson first started the club and he later met him, and that Joe Louis got in with Bill Robinson.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yes, my wife will tell you that that was Utopia, that was nth degree entertainment up there.
Did you get much in tips? Did you make much in tips working there?

-- all those waiters. Kid Griffith was the head waiter, and all those other guys like that, they'd get nice tips, they got nice tips, waiters. Oh, that was big time. You know how that place first started? Jack Johnson.
Jack Johnson was the first owner of the Cotton Club.
Did you ever get to meet him?

Yes, I eventually met him after -- in latter days, you know, just acquaintance type. Jack, I want to introduce you to Jimmie Lunsford's drummer, Jimmy -- James Crawford, I was going under. It was a pleasure seeing that old champ.
What kind of a guy was he?
Nice, but he knew who he was. I met -- I knew Joe Louis well, Ray Robinson well, and they were my
Now, people, of course, like Joe Louis, could he come in the Cotton Club?
Well, he wasn't the champion then. He went in with Bill Robertson.
